assets: the configuration registry (config/registry/<owner>/<key>.json) and each owner's generated aggregate
the JSON contracts and their generated types (contracts/)
boundaries: a pull request's change to a registry key and the gate that judges it
the registry and the scripts that read it at run time
a committed generated file and its generator

threats.statement: A key is declared under another owner's name, or written by hand outside scripts/config with a value its schema refuses, so a reader takes a value its owner never set or the registry's API would not have accepted.

A change loosens a budget, a threshold or a lock value so that a later change passes a check it should fail. Residual: only the budgets, the SLOs and the exception lists are tighten-only; any other registry value (a gate threshold, a timeout) changes on the gate's checks alone.
A generated aggregate or type is edited by hand, or a contract changes incompatibly, so readers and writers disagree on what a key or an event holds.
A value changes and nobody can tell which change set it or why.
A secret is stored as a registry value and reaches the public repository. Residual: the shape check catches only values that look like a secret.
A malformed key or an unreadable value makes every script that loads the registry fail, so the gate and the delivery stop.

A change to a key that governs the gate (its allowed workflows, its stages) widens what the gate lets through without a decision. Residual: the rule that asks a gate change for a decision matches the gate's scripts, not config/registry/gate/, and accepts any recorded D-NNN, not one that approves the change.

findings.finding: The statement described a malformed value (tampering); the registry's real spoofing case, a key declared under another owner, was missing though config.check refuses it.
Budgets and exception lists are tighten-only, other thresholds are not; the statement implied all are.
The flagged residual (the shape check catches only secret-shaped values) is honest.
findings.reason: kept; a value that does not look like a secret cannot be told from configuration by a check.

findings.finding: STD-commit-check-gate-errors matches gate_pin.GATE_FILE (scripts/gate-*, scripts/lib/gate*, the structure and commit checks): config/registry/gate/*.json, scripts/verify-commit and scripts/lib/verify_commit.py are outside it, so a change to a gate key needs no decision; and any recorded D-NNN satisfies it.
findings.reason: residual added; follow-up: widen GATE_FILE to the gate's registry keys and its GitHub entry point.
